name: M3tering Console
role: Open-source contributor (M3tering Protocol): UI and architecture revamp
summary: Rebuilt the interface and core logic of the M3tering Protocol's service console, the gateway app that bills LoRaWAN smart meters on-chain: a themeable desktop-style UI, a central server that manages many gateways, and one-command deployment.
description: M3tering Console runs on each LoRaWAN gateway. It reads meter reports from ChirpStack, decides whether each meter stays on based on on-chain revenue and price, replies to the meter, and publishes signed transactions to Arweave, Streamr and the prover. I redesigned its whole interface as a desktop-style workspace with windowed apps (Terminal over SSH, ChirpStack, Paint, Settings and UI extensions) in four themes, working on phones as well as desktops. I then added opt-in central and gateway roles: one central login reaches every site, while gateways only make outbound, authenticated connections and keep billing locally when central is away. Billing safety comes first: one durable owner per decision, uncertain outcomes held for reconciliation instead of retried, and no duplicate relay or billing effects. Delivered through upstream PRs #58–#63 (about 19,000 lines added).
highlights: Redesigned the UI as a responsive desktop workspace: draggable, resizable windows, dock and launcher, four themes, touch gestures and keyboard control
Added central and managed-gateway roles: gateway enrollment, credential rotation and revocation, SSH and ChirpStack tunnels, and audit logs
Kept billing safe: atomic transactions and nonces, at-most-once publication, reconciliation of uncertain outcomes, and fail-closed relay decisions
Added signed, paired container updates with health checks and automatic rollback, plus a one-command auto-compose.sh deploy for every role
239 unit and integration tests and 28 Playwright browser tests
